details: Human touch is relative and deceptive.
Touch judgment depends on prior skin condition rather than objective hotness.
experiments_or_examples: Three Beaker Experiment: Dip one hand in cold water A, one in hot water C, then both in lukewarm water B; yields conflicting sensations.

details: Temperature is a reliable measure of the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.
Clinical Thermometer: Measures human body temperature (range 35°C–42°C; normal body temp = 37.0°C). Contains a kink/constriction to prevent liquid drop upon removal.
Digital Thermometer: Uses electronic heat sensors, eliminating toxic mercury risks.
Laboratory Thermometer: Measures experimental liquid temperatures (range -10°C to 110°C). Lacks a kink.
experiments_or_examples: Measuring water temperature during laboratory heating

details: Keep thermometer vertical; submerge bulb fully in liquid without touching container walls.
Position eye level horizontally inline with the top of liquid column to avoid parallax error.
Lab thermometers must be read while immersed.
Weather tracking uses Maximum-Minimum Thermometers to record daily high/low temperatures.
Historical pioneer: Anna Mani contributed significantly to Indian meteorological instruments.
